mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 exceeding 2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained UNRATE > 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 0.5% in both INDPRO and RSAFS indicates a broad-based acceleration in industrial production and retail sales, reflecting strengthening economic activity and supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month +0.5% AND RSAFS > previous month +0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and RSAFS rise by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST below 1400 thousand units for three consecutive months signals weakening housing demand, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST remains below 1400 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above 150,000 for four consecutive months signals robust job creation, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +150,000 for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of PAYEMS increases above 150,000.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative relationship exists between GDPC1 and S&P 500 forward returns: quarterly declines in GDPC1 of more than 1% are associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the following 60 trading days, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter.
